mainTopic: Curdling cheese with an animal's stomach: when the milk inside is forbidden, and the final הלכה that it is mere secretion; then the start of a new משנה on חלב and דם.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a משנה about cheese curdled with an animal's stomach. The milk in an animal's stomach takes the status of the mother it nursed from, because it is only stored inside. רב הונא explains the משנה's 'gentile's stomach' as a goat bought from a gentile. After a challenge from eggs, the worry becomes that it nursed from a common טמאה animal, a worry that applies only to gentiles, who do not separate their animals. שמואל instead reads the line as one case: a gentile's slaughter is נבלה. His opinion is reconciled with his cheese statement by a retraction. The משנה's two clauses, a נבלה's stomach forbidden and a טרפה's permitted, are explained the same way, after רבא rejects רב חסדא's answer. Two reports of רבי יוחנן on rennet are brought, and the הלכה permits the milk inside any of these stomachs, because it is mere secretion. Only the stomach wall of a נבלה is forbidden. A new משנה then begins comparing the strictness of חלב and דם.

steps.title: Curdling with kosher stomach skin: forbidden if it gives flavor
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that cheese curdled with the stomach skin of a kosher animal is forbidden if the skin gives flavor to the milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is enough to give flavor, that cheese is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle. It finishes its rule about someone who curdles cheese using the stomach skin of a kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the animal is kosher, its stomach skin is meat. Mixing it into milk raises a meat-and-milk problem. The cheese becomes forbidden only if the meat's flavor is actually noticeable in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives flavor: the mixed-in item is strong enough to be tasted
It is forbidden

phrases.english: If there is enough to impart flavor –
that [cheese] is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Curdling cheese with kosher stomach skin forbids the cheese if the skin gives flavor.

steps.title: Milk in the stomach follows the animal it nursed from
steps.stepSummary: A kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה has forbidden stomach milk. A טרפה that nursed from a kosher animal has permitted stomach milk, because the milk is only stored inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה: its stomach milk is forbidden. A טרפה that nursed from a kosher animal: its stomach milk is permitted, because the milk is just collected in its insides.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches whose status the milk in an animal's stomach has. It follows the mother it came from, not the animal that drank it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The milk does not become part of the drinking animal's body. It is only sitting inside it, like something stored in a container. So its status comes from where the milk came from.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher animal
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even if properly slaughtered
The stomach (here, the milk curdled inside it, used to make cheese)
Collected in its insides: stored there, not part of its body

steps.whatToRemember: Milk in an animal's stomach takes the status of the animal it nursed from.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the stomach milk follows the animal it is found in. The משנה says the opposite: it follows the mother that supplied the milk.

phrases.english: A kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה –
its stomach [milk] is forbidden.
A טרפה that nursed from a kosher animal –
its stomach [milk] is permitted,
because it is collected in its insides.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁרָה שֶׁיָּנְקָה מִן הַטְּרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a new rule about the milk inside the stomach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stomach milk takes the status of its source animal, because it is only stored in the drinking animal.

steps.title: Isn't a gentile's animal's stomach already נבלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists a gentile's stomach separately from נבלה, when a gentile's slaughter is itself נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that the stomach of a gentile's animal is not נבלה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and questions the wording of an earlier line in the משנה (not in our text), which forbade the stomach of a gentile and of a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal slaughtered by a gentile already counts as נבלה. So listing 'gentile' and 'נבלה' as two separate items seems repetitive. The question pushes us to find a different case for 'a gentile's stomach'.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that follows the משנה
Is that to say...? (introduces a challenge)
An animal that died without proper kosher slaughter
The stomach of a gentile's animal

phrases.english: GEMARA: Is that to say the stomach of a gentile's [animal]
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier line in the משנה that forbids the stomach of a gentile and of a נבלה.

phrases.english: is not נבלה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ קֵבַת גּוֹי לָאו נְבֵלָה הִיא
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's separate listing of 'stomach of a gentile' and 'stomach of a נבלה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gentile's slaughter is already נבלה, so listing it separately looks redundant.

steps.title: רב הונא: a young goat bought from a gentile
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the case is a Jew who bought a young goat from a gentile and slaughtered it properly. The worry is that it nursed from a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Here we are dealing with someone who buys a young goat from a gentile, and we are concerned that it may have nursed from a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. 'A gentile's stomach' does not mean the gentile slaughtered it. It means the animal came from a gentile's herd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat itself is fine, since a Jew slaughtered it. The problem is the milk in its stomach. Following the rule of step 2, that milk takes the status of the mother it nursed from, and in a gentile's herd she might have been a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (defines the case)
A young goat
We are concerned (about a possibility)

phrases.english: רב הונא said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּלוֹקֵחַ גְּדִי מִן הַגּוֹי עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with one who buys a young goat from a gentile,
phrases.notes: He means a Jew bought it and slaughtered it himself, so the meat is not נבלה.

phrases.english: and we are concerned that perhaps it nursed from a טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּלוֹקֵחַ גְּדִי מִן הַגּוֹי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Gentile's stomach' seemed to mean an animal a gentile slaughtered, which would make it the same as נבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a goat bought from a gentile and slaughtered by a Jew, with a worry about where its stomach milk came from.

steps.title: We don't worry about טרפה with gentiles' eggs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: a known teaching allows buying eggs from gentiles without worrying about נבלה or טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really worry that it nursed from a טרפה? But we learned: we may buy eggs from gentiles, and we don't worry about נבלה or טרפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's reason. It brings a source showing that we normally don't worry that something from a gentile came from a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eggs could have come from a hen that was a טרפה, yet we ignore that possibility. By the same logic, we shouldn't worry that the goat nursed from a טרפה. So רב הונא's explanation seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really...? (introduces a challenge)
Eggs

phrases.english: And are we really concerned
that perhaps it nursed from a טרפה?
But didn't we learn: We may buy eggs from gentiles,
and we are not concerned about נבלה
nor about טרפה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא יָנַק מִן הַטְּרֵפָה וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that we worry the goat nursed from a טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The eggs teaching shows we don't worry about a gentile's item coming from a טרפה.

steps.title: The worry is a טמאה animal, not a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises רב הונא's statement: the concern is that the goat nursed from a non-kosher species (טמאה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: we are concerned that perhaps it nursed from a טמאה animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the wording of רב הונא's answer. The worry is not a טרפה but a non-kosher kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of the goat bought from a gentile stays the same. Only the reason for the worry changes: from a kosher animal with a defect (טרפה) to a non-kosher species (טמאה). This avoids the challenge from the eggs.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (corrects an earlier statement)
A non-kosher species of animal

phrases.english: Rather, say:
we are concerned that perhaps it nursed from a טמאה animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא יָנַק מִן הַטְּמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by restating רב הונא's concern.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The concern was that the goat nursed from a טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern is that the goat nursed from a טמאה animal.

steps.title: Why worry about טמאה but not טרפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the טמאה worry different from the טרפה worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about a טרפה, that we don't worry about it, and about a טמאה animal, that we do worry about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the distinction it just made. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are forbidden sources of milk, so the different treatment needs a reason. The question asks what logic separates them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks for the reason behind a distinction)

phrases.english: And what is different about a טרפה, that we are not concerned,
and what is different about a טמאה animal, that we are concerned?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא טְרֵפָה דְּלָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the distinction created in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason we worry about טמאה but not about טרפה.

steps.title: טרפה is rare; טמאה is common
steps.stepSummary: The answer: טרפה animals are uncommon, but non-kosher animals are common, so we worry about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טרפה is not common; a טמאה animal is common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is how often each one happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We don't worry about rare possibilities, which is why the eggs from gentiles are allowed. A gentile's herd often includes non-kosher animals, so it is realistic that the goat nursed from one. That is why its stomach milk is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Common, frequent
Not common, rare

steps.whatToRemember: The stomach of a goat bought from a gentile is forbidden. The worry is that it nursed from a common non-kosher animal (טמאה), not from a rare טרפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule: we worry about possibilities that are common, not ones that are rare.

phrases.english: A טרפה is not common,
a טמאה animal is common.

steps.triggerLanguage: טְרֵפָה לָא שְׁכִיחָא טְמֵאָה שְׁכִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We only worry about common possibilities. A טרפה is rare, while non-kosher animals are common.

steps.title: If it is common, why not worry about our own animals too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 8: if young animals often nurse from non-kosher animals, that should worry us even with animals owned by Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is so common, let us worry even about our own animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer that nursing from a טמאה animal is common. If it is common, the worry should apply to Jewish-owned animals too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said we worry about a טמאה but not a טרפה because non-kosher animals are common. But being common is a fact about animals, not about who owns them. So why limit the worry to an animal bought from a gentile?

keyTerms.meaning: Common, happens often
Let us worry about it, let us be concerned
With our own (animals), with what belongs to us

phrases.english: If it is common,
phrases.notes: "It" means a young animal nursing from a non-kosher animal, from step 8.

phrases.english: then let us worry even about our own animals!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שְׁכִיחָא, אֲפִילּוּ גַּבֵּי דִּידַן נֵיחוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in step 8 (non-kosher animals are common).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that we worry about טמאה because it is common.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the worry comes from how common it is, it should apply to all animals, including Jewish-owned ones, not only to animals bought from gentiles.

steps.title: Jews keep their animals apart from non-kosher ones; gentiles do not
steps.stepSummary: Jews keep away from non-kosher animals and separate their young animals from them, so the חכמים made no גזרה for them. Gentiles do not, so the חכמים made a גזרה about their animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: We keep away from non-kosher animals, and when we see them we separate them, so the חכמים did not decree about us. They do not keep away from them, and when they see them they do not separate them, so the חכמים decreed about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that what matters is how the owner behaves. Jews pull their animals away from non-kosher ones, and gentiles do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-kosher animals are common everywhere, but a Jewish owner actively keeps his kosher young animals away from them. A gentile owner has no reason to do this. So the חכמים made a גזרה only on an animal bought from a gentile.

keyTerms.meaning: We keep apart, we stay away
We separate (them), we pull them away
The חכמים made a decree (גזרה)

steps.whatToRemember: The worry about nursing from a non-kosher animal applies only to animals from gentiles, because Jews keep their animals away from non-kosher ones.

phrases.english: We, who keep away from them,
and when we see them, we separate our animals from them,
the חכמים did not make a decree about them.
They, the gentiles, who do not keep away from them,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי חָזוּ לְהוּ לָא מַפְרְשִׁי לְהוּ –
phrases.english: and when they see them, do not separate their animals from them,
the חכמים made a decree about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן דְּבָדְלִינַן מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the behavior of the owner
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since nursing from non-kosher animals is common, the worry should apply to all animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: How common it is matters only when the owner does not separate his animals. Jews do separate them, so the גזרה applies only to gentiles' animals.

steps.title: שמואל reads the משנה as one case: a gentile's slaughter is נבלה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב הונא's reading. He says the משנה teaches only one law: the stomach of an animal slaughtered by a gentile is נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The משנה teaches one case: the stomach of an animal slaughtered by a gentile is a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's different way of reading the משנה. He says it is not two separate cases but one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא (step 4) read the gentile's case as a separate case, a goat bought from a gentile and properly slaughtered. שמואל says the משנה simply explains why the gentile's stomach is forbidden: a gentile's slaughter makes the animal a נבלה. So the milk in the stomach is forbidden because it belongs to a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches one (case), not two
Stomach (here, with the curdled milk inside it)
Slaughter done by a gentile
An animal that died without kosher שחיטה, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
The משנה teaches one case:
the stomach of an animal slaughtered by a gentile is a נבלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: חֲדָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב הונא's approach and offers a different reading of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה teaches a single case: the stomach of an animal slaughtered by a gentile is forbidden as נבלה.

steps.title: שמואל's statement about gentile cheese seems to contradict him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל really holds this. Elsewhere he said gentile cheese was forbidden because it is curdled with the skin of a נבלה's stomach, which suggests the stomach contents themselves are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did שמואל really say this? Didn't שמואל say: Why did they forbid gentiles' cheese? Because they curdle it with the skin of a נבלה's stomach. That implies the stomach contents themselves are permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one statement of שמואל against another. His cheese statement seems to say the milk inside a נבלה's stomach is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 שמואל forbids the stomach contents of a gentile's slaughter because it is נבלה. But in the cheese statement he blames only the stomach skin. That implies the curdled milk inside the stomach is permitted even from a נבלה. So the two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Cheese made by gentiles
They curdle (the milk to make cheese)
The skin (lining) of the stomach
Is permitted

phrases.english: But did שמואל really say this?
But didn't שמואל say:
Why did they forbid the cheese of gentiles?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ בְּעוֹר קֵבַת נְבֵלָה.
phrases.english: Because they curdle it with the skin of a נבלה's stomach.
This implies that the stomach contents themselves are permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's statement in step 11 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading that the stomach of a gentile's slaughter is forbidden as נבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's cheese statement blames only the stomach skin, which implies the milk inside a נבלה's stomach is permitted. That contradicts forbidding it as נבלה.

steps.title: One ruling is from before a change of opinion, the other from after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction: the משנה's ruling comes from before a retraction, and שמואל's cheese statement comes from after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here it is before the retraction, and there it is after the retraction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. The two statements reflect two stages of the law, before and after an opinion was changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, which forbids the milk inside a נבלה's stomach, follows the earlier opinion. שמואל's cheese statement follows the later opinion, which permitted that milk itself. So שמואל is explaining each source according to its own stage, and he does not contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no contradiction
A retraction, going back on an earlier opinion

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל reads the משנה as forbidding a gentile's slaughter as נבלה. This fits the opinion before the retraction, while his cheese statement fits the opinion after it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל changed his own mind. The retraction is a change in the earlier ruling about the milk in a נבלה's stomach, and each of שמואל's statements matches a different stage.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, in the משנה, it is before the retraction,
phrases.notes: This points to a retraction about gentile cheese that is told about elsewhere (עבודה זרה כט:).

phrases.english: there, in שמואל's cheese statement, it is after the retraction.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן – קוֹדֶם חֲזָרָה, כָּאן – לְאַחַר חֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two stages of the law (before and after a retraction)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל contradicts himself about whether the milk inside a נבלה's stomach is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה reflects the opinion before the retraction (forbidden), and the cheese statement reflects the opinion after it (permitted). There is no contradiction.

steps.title: The משנה permits a טרפה's stomach but forbids a נבלה's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a טרפה's stomach milk is permitted, then asks how this fits with the first clause, which forbids the stomach of a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה (and the rest of that line: a טרפה that nursed from a kosher animal, its stomach milk is permitted). But the first clause of the משנה says the stomach of a gentile's animal and of a נבלה is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. It points out that this line seems to clash with the משנה's own first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later clause permits the milk in a טרפה's stomach, because that milk is only collected inside it and is not part of its body. By that reasoning, the milk in a נבלה's stomach should also be permitted. Yet the first clause forbids it, so the two clauses of the same משנה seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The stomach of a young animal, holding curdled milk; it was used to make cheese
An animal with a fatal defect; it is not kosher even if properly slaughtered
An animal that died without a proper kosher slaughter
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: A kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה's line: a טרפה that nursed from a kosher animal has permitted milk in its stomach.

phrases.english: But doesn't the first clause teach:
The stomach of a gentile's animal and of a נבלה
is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה and sets it against the משנה's first clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the milk in a טרפה's stomach is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later clause permits a טרפה's stomach milk because the milk is only collected inside it. That same reason should permit a נבלה's stomach milk, yet the first clause forbids it.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the נבלה rule is only about how it looks
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the first clause forbids a נבלה's stomach only because eating from it looks like eating carcasses. A טרפה was at least slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: in the first clause, someone eating from the stomach looks like a person who eats carcasses. Here, with a טרפה, there was a slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The two cases differ because of how eating from them looks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, the milk in a נבלה's stomach is not truly forbidden in itself. It is forbidden only because eating it looks disgusting, like eating carcasses. A טרפה went through שחיטה, so eating its stomach milk does not look as bad, and it stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He looks like someone who eats carcasses
Kosher slaughter of an animal

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
In the first clause, he looks like one who eats carcasses;
here, there is a slaughter.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the טרפה case. The animal was properly slaughtered, even though it is still not kosher to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases by how eating from them looks
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נבלה and a טרפה are both non-kosher, so their stomach milk should have the same law.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נבלה's stomach is forbidden only because eating it looks like eating carcasses. A טרפה was slaughtered, so that concern does not apply.

steps.title: רבא: a טרפה should be stricter, not more lenient
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues with a קל וחומר that a slaughtered טרפה should be forbidden even more than a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Isn't it the other way around, and even more so? A נבלה is disgusting, so even if you permit its stomach, people will not come to eat its meat, and still you said it is forbidden. A slaughtered טרפה is different: if you permit its stomach, people will come to eat from it. Shouldn't it be forbidden all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב חסדא's answer. He argues that the logic actually points the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People find a נבלה disgusting, so allowing its stomach would not lead anyone to eat its meat. A slaughtered טרפה looks like normal meat, so allowing its stomach milk could lead people to eat the meat itself. If the less risky נבלה is forbidden, the riskier טרפה should surely be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; the 'how much more' logic of a קל וחומר
Disgusting, repulsive
You permit

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But isn't it all the more so?
phrases.notes: רבא means the reasoning should make the טרפה forbidden all the more, the opposite of what רב חסדא said.

phrases.english: Just as a נבלה, which is disgusting,
so that if you permit its stomach,
people will not come to eat from it,
and you said no, it is forbidden;
a slaughtered טרפה,
where if you permit, people will come to eat from it,
is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו כֹּל דְּכֵן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's answer from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the slaughter of a טרפה makes its stomach milk more lenient
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if a disgusting נבלה, which carries little risk, is forbidden, then a slaughtered טרפה, which might lead people to eat its meat, should be forbidden even more.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the משנה rules that a טרפה is forbidden. He is saying רב חסדא's reason cannot explain why the משנה permits it.

steps.title: Before and after the retraction; a משנה stays in place
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק, quoting רבי יוחנן, says the two clauses come from different times, before and after the retraction. The older clause stayed in the משנה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: there is no difficulty. This clause is from before the retraction, and that clause is from after the retraction. A משנה does not move from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב חסדא's answer fell, the גמרא gives a new answer to the question from step 14. The two clauses simply come from two different stages of the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause, forbidding a נבלה's stomach, reflects the ruling from before the retraction. The later clause, permitting a טרפה's stomach milk, reflects the ruling from after it. Once a משנה was taught it was not erased, so the older ruling stayed next to the newer one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is given
It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
A retraction, when a sage takes back his earlier ruling
A משנה does not move from its place; an older ruling is left in the text even after the law changes

steps.whatToRemember: The two clauses of the משנה reflect two stages of the law, from before and after the retraction. The older clause was never removed, because a משנה is not changed once it is taught.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a משנה can hold an outdated ruling next to a newer one. A contradiction between its clauses can sometimes be explained by timing instead of by a difference in reasoning.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is not difficult:
here, it is from before the retraction;
phrases.notes: This is the same retraction the גמרא mentioned just before (step 13). 'Here' means the first clause, about the נבלה.

phrases.english: there, it is from after the retraction;
and a משנה does not move from its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's answer, which רבא rejected in step 16, with a new answer to the question from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two time periods: before and after a retraction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses reflect the same law at the same time, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is from before the retraction and the later clause is from after it. The first clause was left in place because a משנה is not changed once taught.

steps.title: First report: a carcass's stomach is fine, but not one from a non-Jew's slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: you may curdle milk with rennet from a נבלה's stomach, but not with rennet from an animal slaughtered by a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: You may use the stomach of a dead, unslaughtered animal to curdle milk. But you may not use the stomach of an animal that a non-Jew slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new statement of רבי יוחנן about which stomachs may be used to make cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds backwards at first. A נבלה was never slaughtered at all, yet it is allowed, while an animal a גוי slaughtered is forbidden. That surprise is exactly what the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: We curdle (milk into cheese)
The stomach (whose contents are used as rennet)
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
An animal slaughtered by a non-Jew

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
One may curdle milk with the stomach of carcasses,
phrases.notes: He means the milky rennet taken from inside the stomach, which makes milk turn into cheese.

phrases.english: but one may not curdle with the stomach of an animal slaughtered by a non-Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the retraction about the משנה's clauses to a new ruling of רבי יוחנן about rennet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rennet from a נבלה's stomach is permitted. Rennet from an animal slaughtered by a גוי is forbidden.

steps.title: This ruling only fits רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר אבא asks whose view this follows. He answers that it must be רבי אליעזר, who holds that a גוי slaughters for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בר אבא said before him: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי אליעזר's, who said that a non-Jew's ordinary intention is for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: A listener points out that רבי יוחנן's ruling only makes sense according to רבי אליעזר. That suggests the ruling rests on a view that is not the mainstream one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלה is only forbidden to eat, so the milk inside its stomach is not caught by the איסור. But if a גוי's slaughter counts as an offering to עבודה זרה, the animal is forbidden even to benefit from. That stricter איסור reaches the stomach contents too.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (Whose view does this follow?)
A non-Jew's ordinary, unstated intention is for idol worship
Idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the issue is how well the גוי slaughtered. The problem is his presumed intention: according to רבי אליעזר, it makes the animal an idol offering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon bar Abba said before him:
According to whom?
According to Rabbi Eliezer,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר סְתָם מַחְשֶׁבֶת גּוֹי לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: who said: a non-Jew's ordinary intention is for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא: כְּמַאן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of the ruling in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling forbidding rennet from a גוי's slaughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling only works if a גוי's slaughter is presumed to be for עבודה זרה, which is רבי אליעזר's view alone.

steps.title: Yes, of course it follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא replies: who else could it follow? He accepts that the ruling is based on רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then according to whom else would it be?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא agrees openly. Yes, this ruling follows רבי אליעזר, and there is no other way to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not push back. He admits the ruling depends on רבי אליעזר. So this report shows רבי יוחנן holding like רבי אליעזר, and that sets up the different report in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, according to whom else? (Meaning: obviously this one)

phrases.english: He said to him:
Rather, according to whom?
phrases.notes: He means: obviously it's רבי אליעזר. Who else could it be?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאֶלָּא כְּמַאן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 19 by agreeing with it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling does follow רבי אליעזר, and there is no alternative explanation.

steps.title: Second report: both stomachs are permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק reports a different version of רבי יוחנן's view. Both a נבלה's stomach and a גוי's slaughter are permitted, and we ignore רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב שמואל בר רב יצחק came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: You may curdle milk with the stomach of a carcass and also with the stomach of an animal a non-Jew slaughtered. We do not worry about רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, more lenient report of what רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי יוחנן does not accept that a גוי slaughters for עבודה זרה. So an animal slaughtered by a גוי is only a regular נבלה. Its stomach contents are permitted, just like a נבלה's.

keyTerms.meaning: When [so-and-so] came (from ארץ ישראל, bringing a teaching)
Both... and...
Not to be concerned for (a view)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One may curdle both with the stomach of a carcass
and with the stomach of an animal slaughtered by a non-Jew,
so as not to be concerned for the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rennet from both a נבלה and a גוי's slaughter is permitted. רבי אליעזר's presumption is not followed.

steps.title: The final ruling: stomach skin is forbidden, but the milk inside is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is: you may not curdle with the skin of a נבלה's stomach. But you may use the stomach contents of a נבלה, of a גוי's slaughter, and of a כשרה animal that nursed from a טרפה. All the more so, you may use those of a טרפה that nursed from a כשרה. The reason is that the milk in the stomach is just a secretion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: You may not curdle milk with the skin of a carcass's stomach. But you may curdle with what is inside a carcass's stomach, inside the stomach of an animal a non-Jew slaughtered, and inside the stomach of a kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה. All the more so, you may use what is inside a טרפה's stomach if it nursed from a kosher animal. Why? The milk gathered in the stomach is just a secretion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling and explains why it is so lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stomach wall is real meat of the forbidden animal, so it is forbidden. The milk inside is treated as mere waste, not food, so the איסור of the animal does not reach it. This also follows the second report: a גוי's slaughter is permitted, and רבי אליעזר's view is not followed.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical law is
The skin (wall) of the stomach itself
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden even if slaughtered
All the more so
What is the reason?
A secretion or waste matter, not real food

steps.whatToRemember: The stomach wall of a נבלה is forbidden. The milk inside any of these stomachs is permitted, because it is only פירשא. A גוי's slaughter is treated like a נבלה here, and רבי אליעזר's view is not followed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the stomach itself with what is inside it. Only the skin of the stomach is forbidden. The rennet-milk inside is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling on kosher rennet. It rests on the rule that stomach milk is a secretion, not part of the animal.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
One may not curdle with the skin of the stomach of a carcass,
but one may curdle with the stomach of a carcass,
and with the stomach of an animal slaughtered by a non-Jew,
and with the stomach of a kosher animal that nursed from a tereifa,
and all the more so with the stomach of a tereifa
that nursed from a kosher animal.
What is the reason?
The milk gathered in it
is merely a secretion.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: אֵין מַעֲמִידִין בָּעוֹר קֵבַת נְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the practical law, following the lenient report of step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only the stomach wall of a נבלה is forbidden for curdling. The milk inside the stomach of a נבלה, a גוי's slaughter, or a טרפה-related animal is permitted, because it is mere secretion.

steps.title: New משנה: Fat and Blood Are Each Stricter in Some Ways
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that חלב is stricter than דם in some ways, and דם is stricter than חלב in others. It then starts listing the ways חלב is stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There is a stricter side to fat compared with blood, and a stricter side to blood compared with fat. The stricter side of fat is that fat...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is setting up a two-sided comparison between חלב and דם, and it starts the list of ways חלב is stricter. That list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both חלב and דם are forbidden by the תורה. Still, the משנה says neither one is simply stricter overall. Each has its own areas where it is the more serious prohibition. This opening line is only the framework, and the specific details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה text.
A stricter side, or a way one law is more severe than another.
Certain fats of a kosher animal that the Torah forbids eating.
Blood, which the Torah forbids eating.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה works in both directions: חלב is stricter in some ways and דם is stricter in others. Keep track of which list you are in as the details come.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the first line as saying חלב is stricter overall. The משנה says each one is stricter in different ways.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
There is a stringency in fat over blood,
and a stringency in blood over fat.
The stringency in fat is that fat...
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here. The rest of the list continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חוֹמֶר בַּחֵלֶב מִבַּדָּם, וְחוֹמֶר בַּדָּם מִבַּחֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the conclusion about curdling milk with a נבלה's stomach in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חלב and דם each have ways in which one is stricter than the other. The משנה begins listing the ways חלב is stricter.
